inputs: a 20-letter phrase repeated at a distance of 30 under the keyword LEMON, and the same phrase at a distance of 29
expected: the source prints that repeated portions of plaintext encrypted with the same portion of the keyword give identical ciphertext segments; at distance 30 (a multiple of 5) the two segments must be identical and at distance 29 they must differ
limitations: A constructed short case designed to isolate the stated condition.

inputs: the 1603 repeated 4-letter windows in the Vigenere ciphertext of the 4598-letter sample under LEMON, their distances, and the factors of those distances
expected: the source expects the distances to be multiples of the keyword length, acknowledges coincidental repeats, and states that the largest factor occurring most commonly is the most likely length; the ranking must therefore put 5 on top, which is the period planted without telling the analysis
limitations: One planted period on one sample. 9 of 1603 distances were coincidental, which is the caveat the same paragraph prints.

inputs: the same ciphertext auto-correlated at lags 1..10, counting the positions where the letters agree
expected: Example 7.77 prints that lags that are multiples of the period show noticeably higher counts; the multiples of the planted 5 must stand out above the mean of the others
limitations: A second route to the same planted period on the same sample; it agrees with the distance analysis rather than replacing it.

inputs: the same segment-and-factor analysis applied to a ciphertext whose key is as long as the message and does not repeat, set against the repeating-keyword case
expected: the source prints that running-key ciphers prevent cryptanalysis by the Kasiski method; the measure is the number of repeated 4-letter windows against what randomness alone would give, C(W,2)/26^4 = 2.45 for 1500 letters. Measured: the repeating-keyword ciphertext yields 164 windows (66.9 times chance) with 5 on top of the factor ranking; the drawn running key yields 2; twenty further key streams with no period yield 0 to 7 each, mean 2.7, i.e. chance level, and their top factors are coincidences among a couple of distances rather than a keyword length
limitations: The key streams here are generated rather than taken from a book; each is verified to have no period, which is the property the claim rests on, and single-window counts of 0 to 7 are small samples where a factor ranking would be meaningless anyway. The source also warns that a redundant key can still fall to statistical attack.
